edges.description: The germline variant is the first hit; the tumour acquires a second, somatic missense variant in the RNase IIIb domain of the other allele. Both hits were found in the cystic nephroma of a family carrying a germline truncating variant, and in an infant's cystic nephroma with anaplastic foci, read by its authors as a nascent anaplastic sarcoma, which carried a germline frameshift and a somatic missense variant.

The germline variant also predisposes to the other DICER1-related tumours, pleuropulmonary blastoma among them: cystic nephroma occurs in about 10% of families with that lung tumour, and both tumours have occurred in one child.

DICER1 is the ribonuclease that processes microRNA precursors, and the hotspot variants hit its RNase IIIb domain. In one pleuropulmonary blastoma with a somatic RNase IIIb missense variant, studied in its tumour and a cell line, 5p-derived microRNA transcripts retained precursor loop sequences that DICER1 normally removes. The 2019 neoplasm-risk study calls the hotspot variants hypomorphic (reduced RNase IIIb function), and the 2017 report of a family's tumours calls the acquired activity neomorphic. No cited source describes what the variant does to microRNA processing in cystic nephroma itself.

How disturbed microRNA processing gives rise to the cystic tumour is not established. The 2010 study of familial cases read its findings as further evidence that microRNA dysregulation takes part in tumour formation.
The tumour may present as a palpable mass.
The tumour can present with non-specific symptoms such as abdominal pain; how it produces them is not described.
The tumour can present with blood in the urine; how it produces it is not described.

The cystic tumour is presumed to be the benign precursor of anaplastic sarcoma of the kidney, and sarcoma arising within cystic nephroma has been described. How often this happens is not known from the cited sources.

nodes.description: The tumour itself: a benign, typically multicystic tumour of the kidney in young children, thought to originate from metanephric tissue. It was bilateral in 9 of 167 published cases (5.4%). A 2014 series noted two views of cystic nephroma: the benign end of a spectrum with cystic partially differentiated nephroblastoma and Wilms tumour, or a mixed epithelial and stromal tumour. The adult tumour is now placed with mixed epithelial and stromal tumour, and a 2021 review reports that one group has classed the childhood tumour, which often carries DICER1 mutations where cystic partially differentiated nephroblastoma does not, as a separate entity rather than part of a spectrum with it.

nodes.description: A heterozygous germline DICER1 variant, predicted to inactivate the allele. In the two families with several cases of cystic nephroma studied in 2010, both variants created premature stop codons, predicted to remove the ribonuclease and double-stranded RNA-binding domains; among the published cases reviewed in 2021, all 12 children with cystic nephroma who had germline testing carried a DICER1 variant. The tumour also carries a second, somatic DICER1 hit.

nodes.description: Surgery is the main treatment: among the published cases, 121 had a radical nephrectomy and 28 nephron-sparing surgery (the type was not given for 16). Removing the tumour may also prevent its progression to sarcoma.

Finding the tumour early, as kidney screening of carrier children aims to, may allow less extensive surgery that spares nephrons and preserves kidney function, especially when disease is bilateral. Nephron-sparing surgery was used in 28 of the published cases.

Another tumour before, with or after the cystic nephroma in 26 of 167 published cases (about 16%): 4 before it, 14 at the same time and 8 after it. The review describes them as DICER1-related tumours, such as pleuropulmonary blastoma, multinodular goitre, embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma and ciliary body medulloepithelioma.

nodes.description: Malignant change of the cystic tumour into anaplastic sarcoma of the kidney, a DICER1-associated sarcoma that is a disease of its own. Cystic nephroma is diagnosed years before the sarcoma (median age 2 years in the 2024 carrier cohort, against 8.7 years in the largest series of the sarcoma), which suggests that it may develop long before malignant progression.

nodes.description: The transforming event: a somatic DICER1 variant in the tumour, typically a missense variant at a hotspot in the RNase IIIb domain of the remaining allele. In a series of 20 childhood cystic nephromas, DICER1 loss-of-function and RNase IIIb hotspot missense variants occurred at rates similar to those in pleuropulmonary blastoma. Some DICER1-related tumours carry both variants in the tumour only, without a germline variant.
